proofText: i told Marcus, "send me the lease before three." then i kept walking.
assistant: Draft for Marcus is ready. Want me to send it?
captionB: i said one sentence while walking.
captionE: this is what i want AI to be.
voice: uh, i am done opening chatbots. like, genuinely done. i said one sentence while walking: Marcus needs the lease before three. and later the follow-up was just sitting there, ready. not sent. not pretending to be me. just, hey, do you want this handled. that is the whole product. not another inbox. less inbox.

hook: if it can spend money, it should be terrified.
proofText: i said, "just pay the invoice." it refused until i approved the exact amount.
assistant: $4,200 invoice found. I will not pay this without you.
captionA: if it can spend money, it should be terrified.
voice: i do not want an AI that is brave with my money. i want it kind of scared. i said, um, just pay the invoice, whatever. it found the four thousand two hundred dollar amount and stopped. no cute autonomy. no little surprise charge. it asked me first. honestly, that is the first moment i trusted it.

hook: the microphone is not the product.
proofText: it ignored the rant and kept the one sentence that had a real action.
assistant: I ignored the rant. Saved only: follow up with Dana.
captionA: the microphone is not the product.
captionE: i care about that more than the hardware.
voice: small cough. the microphone is not the product. the boundary is. because if i complain about traffic for forty seconds, i do not want a database of my little breakdown. i want that deleted. but if i say, remind Dana after lunch, that should survive. that line, that separation, is the product.

hook: my calendar is lying to me.
proofText: the meeting was one block. the real work was five tiny promises after it.
assistant: I found 5 follow-ups from the call. None were calendar events.
captionA: my calendar is lying to me.
captionB: the meeting is not the work.
captionE: this is the part i need caught.
voice: my calendar is lying to me. it says the meeting was thirty minutes. no. the meeting was thirty minutes and then five little debts: send the deck, text Corey, book the room, remember the allergy thing, follow up Friday. those are not events. they are the part that makes you look unreliable when you miss them.

hook: i do not need another productivity app.
proofText: most apps quietly make you manage the app too.
boundaryLines: does not ask you to organize
assistant: You said it once. I kept the obligation, not the noise.
captionA: i do not need another productivity app.
captionC: do not give me app homework.
voice: i do not need another productivity app. i already have homework. every app is like, organize your life in here. tag it. sort it. maintain it. no. that is just admin with nicer fonts. i want to say the thing once, in normal words, and have the obligation come back when it matters.

hook: parents need this more than founders.
proofText: school form, pickup time, dentist reschedule, cereal, birthday gift.
assistant: School form is ready. Pickup stays at 2:45. Want me to text Maya?
captionA: parents need this more than founders.
captionC: for the form you remembered in the car.
voice: parents need this more than founders. sorry, but they do. it is not glamorous. it is the school form you remember in the car, the pickup time, the dentist reschedule, the cereal, the birthday gift for a kid you barely know. that is the real operating system. and people are doing it from memory, which is insane.

hook: most agents have no social judgment.
proofText: doing the task is easy. knowing whether to do it is the whole thing.
assistant: This involves another person. I drafted it, but I need your yes.
captionA: most agents have no social judgment.
captionC: knowing whether to do it is hard.
voice: most agents have no social judgment. and that sounds mean, but it is true. doing the task is the easy part. knowing whether to do it is the product. act on the boring safe stuff. ask when another human is involved. hard stop on money. and sometimes, honestly, just shut up.

hook: my phone became a guilt rectangle.
proofText: every unlock is a tiny reminder that i owe somebody something.
assistant: You owe Nina the address. I can send it now or hold it.
captionA: my phone became a guilt rectangle.
captionB: every unlock has a debt in it.
voice: my phone became a guilt rectangle. every time i unlock it, i remember i owe somebody something. not something huge. just, send Nina the address, answer the lease thing, cancel the trial. tiny debts. i do not want another app yelling at me. i want one clean ask, at the right time, before the debt gets weird.

hook: the intro i almost forgot was worth more than the app.
proofText: i promised a double opt-in, then immediately lost it in the day.
assistant: Double opt-in draft is ready. I kept it warm, not pushy.
captionA: the intro i almost forgot was worth more than the app.
voice: the intro i almost forgot was probably worth more than the app subscription. that is the annoying part. social capital leaks quietly. you say, yeah, i will double opt-in you to Sam. then the day eats it. no task. no calendar. just a little promise sitting in your reputation. that is exactly what i want caught.

hook: if this sounds boring, you probably need it.
proofText: it is not a robot friend. it is a second short-term memory with brakes.
assistant: I remember the thing you meant to do. I will still ask before I act.
captionA: if this sounds boring, you probably need it.
voice: if this sounds boring, you probably need it. it is not a robot friend. it is not a magic girlfriend. it is a second short-term memory with brakes. the thing you meant to do comes back. the risky stuff asks first. the money stops. if that feels obvious, uh, that is basically the preorder filter.
